was: RV campground in the pines above the Little Muskegon River near Morley; water/electric (30/50A) and full-hookup back-in and pull-through sites with concrete pads, rustic tent sites incl. on the river. Campspot June 2027 weeknight: W/E $50, FHU $54. RV Life 4*/$$$ ~$44/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude
note: Campground beside the Little Muskegon River near Morley, with something going on every weekend: kids' crafts, games, theme weekends, cornhole, dance parties and karaoke.  A swimming pool opens from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day weekend, and there is a jump pad, mini-golf, a basketball court, a game room and rec room, and a large picnic area by the river.  It has an LP fill station and delivers firewood and ice to the site, and bikers on the White Pine Bike Trail get special rustic rates Sunday to Thursday.  Cabins and park models are rented. --Claude

was: Family-owned campground in the woods along Duke Creek (designated trout stream) 18 mi north of Grand Rapids near Cedar Springs; ~114 sites: water/electric and full-hookup RV sites (20/30/50 amp, pull-throughs, creekside FHU), tent sites, cabins and park models; pool, weekend activities; weekend, weekly or seasonal stays. 2026 operator rates (family of 5): W/E nightly $48; Campspot June 2027 weeknight: W/E $48, 20/30A FHU $50, 50A pull-through $55, creek-side FHU $58. RV Life 4*/$$$ ~$43/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude
note: Campground in natural woods along Duke Creek, an official trout stream (fishing needs a license), 18 miles north of Grand Rapids in Cedar Springs.  Every weekend brings arts and crafts, an activity, a penny dive and a wagon ride, and there are hiking trails and a pool with no lifeguard on duty.  Sites have a fire ring and a picnic table but no grill.  Aggressive dog breeds aren't allowed, nor is outside firewood.  Cabins and park models are also rented. --Claude

was: ~200-site wooded family campground on N Business 31 just south of Pentwater, a mile from Charles Mears State Park and Lake Michigan; W/E, vintage, premium and deluxe full-hookup sites (30/50 amp) incl. pull-throughs, two pools. Campspot June 2027 weeknight: $45 for every RV site type. RV Life 4.5*/$$$ ~$50/night (auto 9/2026); Campspot 5.0 over 62 verified reviews. --Claude
note: Family-owned campground, celebrating 42 seasons, in the wooded dunes 2 miles north of Pentwater, with gated entrances.  AJ's Family Fun Center, inside the campground, has go-karts, mini-golf, an arcade and ice cream.  There are two heated pools (no lifeguard), volleyball, tetherball, ping-pong, hiking, disc golf and a fish-cleaning station, and mobile pump-outs come on Mondays and Fridays.  Log cabins sleep five, and golf carts, ATVs and UTVs aren't allowed in the campground. --Claude

was: RV park on M-55 (Caberfae Hwy) near Wellston in the Manistee National Forest, next to ORV/snowmobile trails; full-hookup sites built for big rigs, 50-amp deluxe trailer sites, smaller 20/30-amp sites for vans/truck campers/small trailers, rustic and tent sites. Campspot June 2027 weeknight: 50A deluxe trailer site $40, FHU $48-53, 30A small-trailer $35. Pin is north of M-55 among the pads; imagery may predate the newer sites. RV Life 4*/$$$ ~$45/night (auto 9/2026); Campspot 4.9 over 13 verified reviews. --Claude
note: RV park in the Manistee National Forest at Wellston, with the Whitetail Party Mart at its entrance, Fawn Crest Golf Course a short walk away, Tippy Dam 3 miles off and Lake Michigan 17 miles west on M-55.  A food truck comes Wednesday to Sunday, and there is a community fire pit, pollinator gardens and digital detox zones, with lighting kept low after 10 p.m.  Its 20-amp sites suit smaller trailers, camper vans, truck campers and pop-ups, there are rustic non-electric sites, and a cottage, a retro trailer and a glamping tent are rented.  The person booking must be 21, seasonal campers go through a background check, and quiet hours run from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. --Claude

was: Franchise Jellystone Park (~200 sites) on N Down River Rd in the jack-pine plains east of Grayling; water/electric and full-hookup RV sites, cabins and RV rentals, pool and themed activities. Campspot June 2027 weeknight: W/E RV site $42, W/E/S $53 (one immediate family per site). Weekend and holiday rates will run higher at a Jellystone. RV Life 4*/$$$ ~$49/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude
note: Franchise Jellystone Park in the woods outside Grayling.  A site may share its water and electric pedestal with another, so extension cords and extra hoses may be needed, and sewer sites are limited.  There is a pool (no lifeguard), a jumping pillow, mini golf, a Silent Disco (new in 2026) and a Bear Factory; day passes cost $15 a person, Sunday to Thursday, and early check-in $35.  The person booking must be 21 and a site holds one immediate family; e-bikes, EV charging and outside firewood aren't allowed, nor are golf carts for overnight guests.  Two dogs at most; quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 8 a.m.  Cabins and RVs are rented. --Claude

was: Wooded campground along Brush Creek near Lawrence (Van Buren Co.); 30- and 50-amp water/electric RV sites, rustic tent/hammock sites, central dump station. There are hiking trails, a playground and fishing; firewood costs $7 a bundle and visitors $5 each.  Generators, fireworks and chainsaws aren't allowed, golf carts, ATVs and UTVs need permission, and quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 8 a.m. --Claude

note: Family campground five miles southwest of downtown Gaylord, near Otsego Lake and thousands of acres of state forest.  It has an indoor pool and spa, an outdoor waterslide, a playground, a stocked trout lake for fishing and an 18-hole mini golf course, plus basketball, horseshoes, kayak rentals and an arcade; a fitness center is being developed.  There are picnic areas and fire pits, cabins and campers are rented, and there is an event venue. --Claude

was: Family campground at Houghton Lake (off W Houghton Lake Dr) in part-to-full shade; electric-only, water+electric and full-hookup (30/50A) back-in and pull-through sites, premium large sites, rustic tent sites, cabins. Campspot June 2027 weeknight: 30A electric-only $39, W/E 30A $42, FHU from $47, premium pull-through FHU $60. RV Life 4.5*/$$$ ~$43/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude
note: Campground near Houghton Lake, Michigan's largest inland lake by surface area, with large wooded sites.  There is a pool (no lifeguard), a fishing pond, basketball, volleyball, horseshoes, a large open playground and a dog run; propane is sold, firewood is delivered to the site, and ORV trails are nearby.  Cabins and a bunk house are rented, there are seasonal sites, and monthly camping is offered after Labor Day.  Outside firewood isn't allowed, and quiet hours run from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. --Claude

was: Small (~17-site) campground on Dutch Settlement Rd near Marcellus (Cass Co.); full-hookup gravel sites, water+electric with greywater, water+electric-only sites (30A breaker, 110 plug - adapters may be needed), primitive tent sites, glamping; booked only through Campspot. Campspot June 2027 weeknight: W/E $40, W/E+greywater $45, FHU $50. RV Life 5*/$$$ ~$48/night (2 reviews) (auto 9/2026); Campspot 5.0 over 43 verified reviews. --Claude
note: Campground in rolling hills near Marcellus, with fishing, hiking and walking trails, a pool and a playground.  RV sites have full hookups on gravel, or water, electric and greywater, with the black tank dumped at the end of the stay; power is a 110-volt plug on a 30-amp breaker, so adapters may be needed.  The Olive Branch camper and the Mustard Seed cabin are rented, there is a primitive tent site, and an extra vehicle costs $5 a day. --Claude

was: Christian non-profit family/youth camp near Hastings (2349 Campground Rd) that rents its wooded campground to the public by the night or week, April 24 - October 11 (2026), booked on Campspot; 30/50-amp RV/tent sites, cabins. Campspot June 2027 weeknight: RV/tent site $15. Camp programs (family camp, teen/kids camps, retreats) run on some weeks. RV Life 5*/$$ ~$30/night (1 review) (auto 9/2026); Campspot 4.8 over 24 verified reviews. --Claude
note: Christian non-profit camp near Hastings that rents campsites and cabins by the day or week alongside its camps and retreats for youth, adults and families.  It has an outdoor pool (Memorial Day to Labor Day), gaga ball pits, basketball, volleyball, tetherball, a playground, a 9-hole frisbee golf course and a nature trail; firewood is $5 a bundle, and seasonal sites cost $1,200 a year.  Tobacco, alcohol and illegal drugs aren't allowed, campers are expected to dress modestly, and quiet hours run from 10 p.m. to 8 a.m. --Claude

was: Family campground on a small lake at 8551 Deep Lake Rd north of Middleville; full-hookup sites with a row of lakeside sites along the shore, cabins, camp store, kayak/canoe/paddleboat rentals, themed events all season. Reservable online. 2026 full hookup (non-lakeside) $45 Sun-Thu, $50 Fri-Sat; lakeside sites cost more; weekly $300. RV Life 4.5*/$$$ ~$43/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude
note: Family campground on Turner Lake, a natural 18-acre lake with a sandy beach (no lifeguard), bordered by state land and close to Deep Lake, Gun Lake and the Yankee Springs Recreation Area.  Some sites are lakeside.  Kayaks, canoes, rowboats and paddleboards rent for $5 an hour on site or $20 an hour off site, and paddleboats for $10 for the first hour and $5 for each hour after; there are hiking trails and a fenced dog park.  Annual events include bingo, crafts, a kayak race, cornhole and fishing tournaments and live music; ice costs $4 a bag and firewood $6 a bundle, which can be delivered to the site.  Golf carts are allowed with a licensed driver 16 or older and insurance, and cabins are rented. --Claude

was: Fishing campground and cabin retreat near Diana in Webster County; a tree-lined creekside lane of full-hookup 30-amp RV sites (#4-10), riverside tent sites, a stocked fishing pond, cabins and glamping, bathhouse; seasonal RV sites too. Booked on Campspot: RV site fitting 45 ft $49.35/night (October 2026 and June 2027 quotes). RV Life 5*/$$$ ~$50/night (auto 9/2026); Google 4.6 over 69 reviews. --Claude
note: Fishing campground and cabin retreat on 22 wooded acres at Diana, a short drive from Webster Springs, where a creek and a river line two sides of the property.  RV sites #4-10 are on a tree-lined creekside lane; sites are level back-ins on gravel and grass, each with a fire ring, and picnic tables are available on request, first come, first served.  Pete's Pond, three acres and stocked, has daily fishing and monthly tournaments, and there are canoes, kayaks, a paddle boat, swimming holes and a hiking trail.  Riverside tent sites, cabins and glamping are also offered, and a small grocery and a diner are down the street.  Pets are allowed for a fee; generators aren't. --Claude

was: Private campground in oak woods outside Fullerton, a summer base for tubing and stock-tank floats: 49 RV sites in tree clearings, water/electric $30 (30-amp) or $40 (50-amp) and full hookups $35-45 a night; primitive tent sites, monthly sites. note: Campground at Fullerton, beneath towering shade trees near the Cedar River.  Overnight guests have river access for fishing and swimming, and the campground runs floats down the Cedar River by reservation: a stock tank for up to 4 people is $100 for 3½ hours, a tube $25 and a kayak $30.  There are jeep trails (open as conditions allow), hiking trails, a playground and summer concerts; portable toilets stand on site, and sites have picnic tables and fire rings.
